governanceNotes: D1 batch 41 (2026-09-24): deferred on three independent grounds. (i) Constitutive identity barrier (ME-41 wrong-identity guard; giant-cell-myocarditis-to-cardiomyopathy rejection precedent): hallux rigidus is, by definition, degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis) of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with painful limitation of dorsiflexion - an identity-to-osteoarthritis edge would assert the diagnosis against its own definition and double-count the same disease (identity-constitutive guard), and unlike flatfoot (batch 34) or Freiberg infraction (batch 35) - where a biomechanical or ischemic process precedes and risks incident osteoarthritis - the osteoarthritis is present at diagnosis rather than downstream. (ii) Wrong-target guard for the documented functional sequelae: the gait and walking-identities (difficulty-walking, gait-abnormality) do not exist in the catalog, so the quantified kinematic outcomes have no correct target (analogous to the batch-40 GBS weakness/respiratory-failure wrong-target screen). (iii) Counter-evidence and zero-record for proximal-overload claims: the Stevens 2022 three-dimensional gait analysis of 16 symptomatic hallux rigidus patients versus 15 controls documents kinematic compensation (increased forefoot supination, reduced hallux motion, smaller step length) with NO significant differences in plantar pressure or plantar loading versus controls - directly undercutting a foot-to-proximal-joint overload chain - and the de Bot 2023 follow-up of 27 patients 22 years after hallux rigidus surgery documents gait parameters and plantar pressures comparable to healthy controls with no clinically significant differences across surgical techniques - no fixed downstream sequela is quantified, and no cohort linking hallux rigidus to incident hip, knee, or ankle osteoarthritis was located in this window (zero-record guard for the compensation-to-proximal-osteoarthritis claim). Negative screens recorded: no unexplained-chronic-pain edge (hallux rigidus pain is localized and explained by the joint diagnosis; the forefoot differential including Morton's neuroma and sesamoiditis is documented but without condition-specific diagnostic-delay quantification - case-matching pain edges require explicit delay or unexplained-presentation documentation, glomus and GTPS precedents distinguishable only where such records exist); no amputation or loss-of-toe edge (rare end-stage surgical outcome without quantification; amputation-of-thumb-fingers-toes remains zero-edge); no depression edge (forefoot-pain mood burden lacks syndrome-specific quantification; zero-record). Sibling scope: hallux-valgus, hammertoe, mallet-toes, and patellofemoral-pain-syndrome remain zero-edge backlog identities with their own windows. Reopening condition: a quantified incident-outcome cohort attributable to hallux rigidus beyond its constitutive joint disease (for example a cataloged difficulty-walking identity with gait-quantified cohorts, or a validated proximal-joint overload cohort), or governance reclassification of the identity away from definitional osteoarthritis.
